correctness.rationale: Complete proof for all n and d. Restriction S^d to S^2 gives a convex Legendre expansion. An exact Laplace-integral inequality controls all Legendre degrees >=8 after the first eight exact values; the coefficients of arcsin cubed have a proved all-order recurrence and an exact odd-square sum bound, proving nonnegative Hilbert-sphere Schoenberg power coefficients for n=1,2,3. At n=4, P6 gives midpoint -17/256; for every n>=5, P2 gives (1-3cos(pi/n)^n)/4<0 by strict monotonicity; on S1, cos(2theta) witnesses all n>=3. The standard-library exact checker passed, but finite tests are not used to infer the infinite statements.

value.rationale: The sharp all-degree boundary for natural geodesic Bernstein covariance approximation is a structural result, not a routine calculation: the operator lifts every source kernel from any S^d with d>=2 to all spheres exactly in its uniform degree range n<=3, while the circle admits only n<=2. This directly addresses the motivating finite-sphere positivity problem in a stronger target sense; exact global witnesses delimit the conclusion. The Legendre sampling restriction plus cubic arcsine coefficient argument provides a potentially reusable mechanism for other angular interpolation schemes.
